narrativeBlocks.title: A bird that starts a quest
narrativeBlocks.body: Ralston summarizes a tale in which a Zhar-Ptitsa steals golden fruit from King Vuislaf's tree. Ivan fails to catch the bird but secures a feather.

narrativeBlocks.title: The collector's caveat
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Ralston's English text; whitespace normalized): “it is a "Chap-book" story, and therefore of doubtful origin.”

narrativeBlocks.title: This is a summary, not the full folktale
narrativeBlocks.body: Ralston explicitly calls this a chapbook story and says its origin is doubtful. Attribute the outline to his discussion rather than presenting it as an ancient pan-Slavic myth.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not collapse the bird variants
narrativeBlocks.body: Ralston compares the Zhar-Ptitsa with the German Golden Bird and notes other variants. Similar motifs do not make every version the same story.
